summary: Kim Lam works in Buddhist and religious studies. Lam held posts at Deakin University's Melbourne Burwood Campus and as a research officer at Western Sydney University.

Kim Plofker is a scholar of Indology and history. She studied at Haverford College and earned her PhD at Brown University under David Pingree. She later held positions at Union College, serving as assistant professor (2007) and associate professor (2019).

Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University in 1992. She served on the Harvard faculty as assistant professor (~1994–2001) and as professor of the comparative and historical study of religion from ~2001.

Kimiaki Tanaka works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Oxford, also studying under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held positions at the University of Tokyo and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Kimmo Koskenniemi is a scholar of computational linguistics who earned his Master of Science at the University of Helsinki (1964–1967). He served at the University of Helsinki as professor of computer linguistics (~1989–2012) and BAULT director (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under the supervision of Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).

King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Lo studied at Fudan University and completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig under Eli Franco, later holding research posts at Leipzig, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and CUHK.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Manchester under the doctoral supervision of Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva was a historian who studied at the University of London (~1958–1961). He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya from ~1969 to 1995.

Kirby Flower Smith was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Maurice Bloomfield and others. He served as professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and directed ASCSA in Rome (1914–1915).

Kirill Solonin is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He served as a professor at Fo Guang University (~2005–2013) and has been a professor at Renmin University of China since ~2013.
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indology scholar who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kishor Chaudhari works in Indology and religious studies. He completed a master's in English at Kavayitri Bahinabai Chaudhari North Maharashtra University in 2013 and became an assistant professor at Government Science College, Chhota Udepur, in 2018.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya and Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, as well as Gopinath Bhattacharya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a doctorate from Kyoto University. He taught at the Fourth Higher School and served as professor of philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973). He served as professor at Shitennoji University and director of the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute.

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Enga Teramoto at Otani University (1927–1931). He held positions at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).

Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Kitaro Nishida (~1917–1920). He later held academic posts at Ryukoku University (~1924–1927) and Otani University (~1925–1927).

Kiyoshi Okano is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. At Kyushu University, he served as associate professor (attested 2002) and as professor in Indian philosophy (attested 2013–2026).

Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He served as a lecturer at Rissho University and as a special researcher at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.
